items.title: 4.8 Theoretical yield, actual yield and percentage yield

source_refs.note: Topic 4.8, printed pages 89-91, as printed: the reasons for a low actual yield, Sample Problem 4.20 and Quick Check 4.10.

blocks.title: Actual yield and theoretical yield
blocks.text: The amount of the products obtained in a chemical reaction is called the actual yield of that reaction. The amount of the products calculated from the balanced chemical equation represents the theoretical yield.
The theoretical yield is the maximum amount of the product that can be produced by a given amount of a reactant, according to balanced chemical equation.
In most chemical reactions the amount of the product obtained is less than the theoretical yield. There are following reasons for that:

items: The processes like filtration, separation by distillation, separation by a separating funnel, washing, drying and crystallization, if not properly carried out, decrease the actual yield.
Some of the reactants might take part in a competing side reaction and reduce the amount of the desired product. So, in most of the reactions the actual yield is less than the theoretical yield.
A reaction may be reversible. Therefore, the amount of the product will be reduced by the backward reaction

blocks.text: A chemist is usually interested in the efficiency of a reaction. The efficiency of a reaction is expressed by comparing the actual and theoretical yields in the form of percentage (%) yield.

blocks.text_alt: % Yield = Actual yield / Theoretical yield x 100

blocks.text: Greater the % age yield, higher will be the efficiency of reaction and vice versa.

blocks.title: Sample Problem 4.20 (% age Yield)
blocks.problem: Aspirin (C₉H₈O₄) is prepared by heating salicylic acid, C₇H₆O₃ (molar mass 138.12 gmol⁻¹) and acetic anhydride, C₄H₆O₃ (molar mass 163.93 gmol⁻¹). C₇H₆O₃ + C₄H₆O₃ → C₉H₈O₄ + CH₃COOH Calculate the theoretical yield of aspirin, (molar mass 180.16 gmol⁻¹) when 3.00 g of salicylic acid is heated with 6.00 g of (CH₃CO)₂O. What is % yield when actual yield is 3.15 g?
steps: Salicylic acid: 1 mol, 138.12 g; Acetic anhydride: 1 mol, 163.93 g; Aspirin: 1 mol, 180.16 g
1mole of Salicylic acid produces aspirin = 1 mol
Number of moles of Salicylic acid = 3.00 g/ 138.12 gmol⁻¹ = 0.022 mol
Number of moles of Salicylic acid = 6.00 g/ 163.93 gmol⁻¹ = 0.037 mol
Here, salicylic acid is limiting reactant while acetic anhydride is an excess reactant. The amount of salicylic controls the yield of product i.e., aspirin.
0.022 mole of Salicylic acid produces aspirin = 0.22 mol
Number of moles of Salicylic acid = Mass of Salicylic acid/ Molar mass of Salicylic acid = 3.00/138.12 = 0.022 mol
0.022 mol Salicylic acid produces Aspirin =0.022 mol
Mass of Aspirin = 0.021 mol x 180.16 g mol⁻¹ = 3.96 g
book_errors: Number of moles of Salicylic acid = 6.00 g/ 163.93 gmol⁻¹ = 0.037 mol

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The molar mass of acetic anhydride, C₄H₆O₃, is 102.09 g mol⁻¹, not 163.93 g mol⁻¹, so its 6.00 g is 6.00 / 102.09 = 0.059 mol (salicylic acid is still the limiting reactant); the 6.00 g line is of acetic anhydride, not salicylic acid. 0.022 mol of salicylic acid gives 0.022 mol of aspirin (not 0.22 mol), and 0.022 mol × 180.16 g mol⁻¹ = 3.96 g (0.021 is a misprint). The question gives an actual yield of 3.15 g, not 2.85 g: % yield = 3.15 / 3.96 × 100 = about 79.5 %.
